title: 古从军行
title_en: An Old Song of Going to War
author: 李颀

text_note.zh: 古籍本“胡鴈”的“鴈”是“雁”的异体字，这里写作“雁”。“野云万里无城郭”，有的版本作“野营万里无城郭”。
text_note.en: The old edition writes the word for wild goose in a variant form; we use the standard form. The line "wild clouds for ten thousand li" reads "camps for ten thousand li" in some editions.

readings.en: Yìn mǎ means to let horses drink, so this character is read yìn here, not yǐn.
In diāodǒu this character is read dǒu.

readings.zh: “雨雪”的“雨”在这里是动词，下的意思，常读 yù。一说读 yǔ，“雨雪”就是雨和雪。
readings.en: Here this character is a verb, meaning to fall, and is often read yù. Another view reads it yǔ, meaning rain and snow.

glosses.zh: 烽火：边境上报警用的火。敌人来了，就在高台上点火。
glosses.en: fēng huǒ: beacon fires on the border, lit on high towers to warn that the enemy is coming.
yìn mǎ: to water the horses.

glosses.zh: 交河：古城名，在今天新疆吐鲁番附近。
glosses.en: Jiāohé: an old town near today's Turpan in Xinjiang.
xíng rén: the soldiers on the march.

glosses.zh: 刁斗：军中的铜锅，白天用来做饭，夜里敲着打更。
glosses.en: diāo dǒu: a bronze pot used in the army, for cooking by day and for beating out the night watches.

glosses.zh: 公主琵琶：汉武帝把一位宗室女子封为公主，嫁给西域的乌孙王，让人在路上弹琵琶给她解闷。琵琶声里满是她远嫁的哀怨。
glosses.en: gōng zhǔ pí pá: Emperor Wu of Han made a girl of the royal clan a princess and sent her to marry the king of Wusun in the far west. Music on the pipa was played to comfort her on the road, and it was full of her sorrow.

glosses.zh: 幽怨：藏在心里的哀愁和怨恨。
glosses.en: yōu yuàn: deep, hidden sorrow and grief.
chéng guō: city walls; here, towns.
hú yàn: wild geese of the northern frontier.

glosses.zh: 胡儿：当地少数民族的士兵。连他们也被苦得流泪。
glosses.en: hú ér: soldiers of the local frontier peoples. Even they weep at this hardship.

glosses.zh: 玉门犹被遮：汉武帝派兵攻打大宛，打得不顺，将领想退兵回来，武帝派人挡住玉门关，说谁敢进关就杀谁。玉门，玉门关，在今天甘肃。
glosses.en: yù mén yóu bèi zhē: when Emperor Wu's army fared badly against Dayuan, its general wanted to retreat. The emperor had the Jade Gate Pass blocked and said anyone who came back through it would be killed. The pass is in today's Gansu.
yīng jiāng: can only take, must stake.

glosses.zh: 逐轻车：跟着将军去拼命。轻车，指汉代的“轻车将军”，这里泛指将领。
glosses.en: zhú qīng chē: to follow the general into battle. Qīng chē recalls the Han title General of Light Chariots, meaning army leaders in general.
huāng wài: the wild, faraway lands beyond the border.

glosses.zh: 蒲桃：就是葡萄。汉代从西域传入中原。
glosses.en: pú táo: grapes. They came to China from the western regions in Han times.

glosses.zh: 汉家：汉朝，这里实际暗指唐朝。
glosses.en: Hàn jiā: the house of Han; here it quietly stands for the Tang.

translation.zh: 白天爬上山，远远望着报警的烽火，
translation.en: By day we climb the hills to watch for beacon fires;

translation.zh: 黄昏时，在交河边给马喝水。
translation.en: At dusk we water our horses by the Jiaohe River.

translation.zh: 风沙昏暗，只听见士兵敲着刁斗打更，
translation.en: In the dark of wind and sand, we hear the watch pot beaten;

translation.zh: 像当年远嫁的公主弹的琵琶，满是哀怨。
translation.en: Like the pipa of the princess sent far away, full of sorrow.

translation.zh: 荒野上云连着云，万里看不到一座城，
translation.en: Wild clouds stretch ten thousand li, with not one town in sight;

translation.zh: 大雪纷纷扬扬，连着无边的沙漠。
translation.en: Snow falls thick and fast across the endless desert.

translation.zh: 北方的大雁夜夜哀叫着飞过，
translation.en: The northern geese cry sadly as they fly, night after night;

translation.zh: 连当地的士兵也一行行地流下眼泪。
translation.en: Even the frontier soldiers' tears fall, pair by pair.

translation.zh: 听说玉门关还被挡着，不许退兵回来，
translation.en: I hear the Jade Gate is still barred, and no one may return;

translation.zh: 只能拿着性命，跟着将军去拼杀。
translation.en: We can only stake our lives and follow the generals on.

translation.zh: 年年打仗，战死的尸骨埋在荒远的边地，
translation.en: Year after year, the bones of the dead are buried in wild lands;

translation.zh: 换来的只是看到葡萄被送进皇宫。
translation.en: All we see in return are grapes brought into the house of Han.

background.zh: 《从军行》是乐府旧题，多写军中生活。李颀在前面加了一个“古”字，表面写汉朝的事，其实是借古讽今。唐玄宗后期常常对边境用兵，很多士兵死在远方。一般认为这首诗就是针对这种情况写的，具体写作年份不能确定。
background.en: "Going to War" is an old yuefu title, usually about army life. Li Qi added the word "old" to it. On the surface the poem is about the Han dynasty, but it really speaks about his own time. In his later years Emperor Xuanzong of Tang often sent armies to the borders, and many soldiers died far from home. The poem is usually read as a protest against this. The exact year it was written is not known.

author_note.zh: 李颀，唐代诗人，大约生活在唐玄宗时期，开元年间考中进士，只做过县尉这样的小官，后来回乡隐居。他和王维、高适、王昌龄等人都有交往。他擅长写边塞诗和七言歌行，这首《古从军行》是他最有名的作品。
author_note.en: Li Qi was a Tang poet who lived around the time of Emperor Xuanzong. He passed the top civil exam in the Kaiyuan era but held only a small county post, and later went home to live quietly. He knew poets such as Wang Wei, Gao Shi and Wang Changling. He was good at frontier poems and long seven-character songs, and this is his best-known work.

appreciation.zh: 诗一开头就是边塞士兵的一天：白天上山看烽火，晚上到河边饮马，日日夜夜都不能放松。夜里风沙昏暗，只有刁斗声和像琵琶一样哀怨的声音。接着视野拉开：万里荒野没有一座城，大雪连着沙漠，大雁在哀叫，连本地人都哭了，何况远离家乡的士兵。后四句点出真正要说的话：皇帝不许退兵，士兵只能拿命去拼；年年都有人战死，埋在荒野里，换来的不过是皇宫里多了一些葡萄。用这么多人的性命，换这么一点小东西，值得吗？诗人没有直接骂，却用最后一句冷冷的对比，把讽刺说得很重。
appreciation.en: The poem opens with a soldier's day on the frontier. By day they climb hills to watch for beacons. At dusk they water horses by the river. They can never relax. At night in the dark wind and sand there is only the watch pot and a sound as sad as a pipa. Then the view widens: ten thousand li of wild land with no town, snow joined to the desert, geese crying. Even the local people weep, so how must soldiers far from home feel? The last four lines say what the poet really means. The emperor will not let the army come back, so the soldiers must risk their lives. Every year men die and are buried in the wilderness. In return, the palace just gets some grapes. Is so many lives worth so small a thing? The poet does not curse anyone. He uses one cold contrast at the end, and the protest hits hard.
